t:
The solution set of the equation
tan⁻¹x−cot⁻¹x=cos⁻¹(2−x) will lie in the
interval
s:
Concept:
For cos⁻¹(θ) to be defined, the argument must satisfy -1 ≤ θ ≤ 1. The domain of the equation restricts the potential solutions.

Calculation:
Domain of cos⁻¹(2 - x):
-1 ≤ 2 - x ≤ 1
Subtract 2: -3 ≤ -x ≤ -1
Multiply by -1: 1 ≤ x ≤ 3

Testing x = 1:
LHS = tan⁻¹(1) - cot⁻¹(1) = π/4 - π/4 = 0
RHS = cos⁻¹(2 - 1) = cos⁻¹(1) = 0
Since LHS = RHS, x = 1 is a solution. 

Because the entire equation is only defined on x ∈ [1, 3], the solution set must lie completely within [1, 3].

Options (A) and (B) are incorrect because the domain is restricted to x ≥ 1, while (D) is incorrect as (C) correctly bounds the solution.

Correct Answer: (C) [1,3]

If a₁,a₂,a₃,……aₙ is an A.P. with common difference d;
(d>0) then
tan[tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₁a₂))+tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₂a₃))+…
……+tan⁻¹(d/(1+aₙ₋₁aₙ))] is equal to
s:
a₁,a₂,…,aₙ are in A.P with common difference d.
a₂=a₁+d
a₃=a₁+2 d
aₙ=a₁+(n−1)d
tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₁a₂))=tan⁻¹((a₂−a₁)/(1+a₁a₂))=tan⁻¹(a₂)−tan⁻¹(a₁)
tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₂a₃))=tan⁻¹((a₃−a₂)/(1+a₂a₃))=tan⁻¹(a₃)−tan⁻¹(a₂)
tan⁻¹(d/(1+aₙ+aₙ))=tan⁻¹((aₙ−aₙ₋₁)/(1+aₙ₋₁aₙ))=tan⁻¹(aₙ)−tan⁻¹(aₙ₋₁)
∴tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₁a₂))+tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₂a₃))+..+tan⁻¹(d/(1+aₙ+aₙ))
=tan⁻¹(aₙ)−tan⁻¹(a₁)
=tan⁻¹((aₙ−a₁)/(1+a₁aₙ))
=tan⁻¹((a₁+(n−1)d−a₁)/(1+a₁aₙ))
=tan⁻¹(((n−1)d)/(1+a₁aₙ))
∴tan{tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₁a₂))+tan⁻¹(d/(1+a₂a₃))+…+tan⁻¹(d/(1+aₙ₋₁aₙ))}
=tan{tan⁻¹(((n−1)d)/(1+a₁aₙ))}
=((n−1)d)/(1+a₁aₙ)
